title: SPMI-style target: sequence start, a header of slave address 5 and command, a register address, then a register write (acknowledged) or read

regs.name: TX
regs.desc: Byte returned for a register read

fields.desc: taken when the register address of a read is complete, sent MSB first

regs.name: RX
regs.desc: Register writes received (data and register address); reading RX frees it

fields.desc: in a command addressed to us

irqs.name: WRITE
irqs.desc: a register write was received (the same clock RX captures it)

notes: sdata (open drain: the target only pulls it low for the ACK and read data) and sclk are the bus pins; they pass through unchanged. Each SCLK phase must last at least three PCLK clocks.

Frame: SSC (SDATA falling while SCLK is high), header {SA[3:0], CMD[3:0]} then the register address, MSB first, sampled on SCLK rising. CMD 0: a data byte follows and the target ACKs it by holding SDATA low for the next bit; CMD 1: the target sends TX on the next 8 bits, each driven from an SCLK fall. Other commands and slave addresses are ignored. This is a simplified SPMI framing: no parity bits, bus park or arbitration.
